children: Our Bureau Mumbai: Dalmia Bharat posted a consolidated loss of 205 crore for the September quarter, weighed down by an exceptional loss of 339 crore related to impairment of certain assets and a separation scheme for eligible employees. The country's fourth-largest cement producer had also reported an exceptional loss in the June quarter.

The 182 crore hit was primarily related to costs associated with its acquisition of cement assets from Jaiprakash Associates. In the September quarter, sales volume rose 3% year-on-year to 7.1 million tonnes, while consolidated revenue from operations increased 4% to 3,563 crore.

Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA), however, fell 29% to 493 crore due to higher costs, particularly for power and fuel. "Demand challenges in few of our key markets along with macro-economic cost headwinds impacted EBITDA for the quarter," chief financial officer Yatin Malhotra said.

Power and fuel costs rose 22% year-on-year to 874 crore, while total expenses increased around 13% to 3,563 crore. "While the operating environment continues to remain challenging, we are hopeful that positive momentum on cement prices and our consistent focus on cost optimisation will help mitigate cost pressure," Malhotra said. EBITDA per tonne of cement fell 31% year-on-year to 698, while net sales realisation rose 1% to 5,042 per tonne.

title: Dalmia Bharat Posts 205cr Loss in Q2 on Exceptional Hit
